_comment: API contract registry. Grouped by app/lib. Updated by sdd-architect (status: defined) and sdd-implementor-back (status: implemented | updated). Source of truth for all endpoints.

_schema._app_keys: Use the app directory name as key. E.g. 'example-api', 'apps/example-app', 'libs/shared-lib'

_update_protocol.create: Set created_in_cycle: N, updated_in_cycle: null, changelog: []. Status: defined (architect) → implemented (implementor-back).
_update_protocol.update: Set updated_in_cycle: N, append to changelog: { cycle: N, date: YYYY-MM-DD, change: 'what changed' }. Status → updated.
_update_protocol.deprecate: Set status: deprecated, append to changelog with change: 'deprecated — reason'

EndpointEntry.spec: path a la spec que lo originó
EndpointEntry.created_in_cycle: número de ciclo donde se definió por primera vez
EndpointEntry.updated_in_cycle: número del último ciclo que lo modificó (null si nunca se actualizó)

responses.200: descripción

endpoints.description: Service health probe. Reports the resolved state of the two engine modules loaded via dynamic import (media-local, composition-remotion/render), the resolution state of the four media binaries (ffmpeg, ffprobe, whisper-cli, the Whisper model) by logical name and env var — never their resolved host path — and the capabilities enabled in this cycle. Answers 200 in both the ok and degraded states. capabilities gains storyboardQueue in spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01. The claude CLI is deliberately NOT added to binaries: that list is resolved by @video-maker/media-local and adding it would report degraded on every machine without Claude Code installed, CI included.

responses.200: application/json: { status: 'ok' | 'degraded', service: 'render-api', cycle: number, time: ISO-8601 string, engine: [{ name, loaded }], binaries: [{ name, envVar, resolved }] (4 entries: ffmpeg, ffprobe, whisper-cli, whisper-model), capabilities (which gained producer in spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: true when the Claude Code binary resolves; it never turns the service degraded, because a machine without Claude Code still renders — same reasoning as D-12 of spec-008 for the binaries list): { renderPipeline, assetStore, jobQueue, montageQueue, storyboardQueue }, jobs: { running, queued } }. status is ok only when every engine module loaded and every binary resolved (all four); the jobs counters never affect it.
responses.405: application/json: { error: { code: 'METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED', stage: null, message, resource, expected } } with an Allow header, for any method other than GET on this path.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

changelog.change: capabilities.assetStore now reports true and cycle now reports 2; the asset store shipped in this cycle does not affect the ok/degraded calculation.

capabilities.jobQueue now reports true, cycle now reports 3, and a new jobs: { running, queued } block reports the runtime queue load. The jobs block is a load counter, not a health signal: it never affects the ok/degraded calculation.

binaries now reports four entries (ffmpeg, ffprobe, whisper-cli, whisper-model) instead of two, and capabilities gains montageQueue: true. cycle is unchanged (D-8, spec-e-burgos-007). status keeps the same ok/degraded formula; it now also degrades when the Whisper model or CLI are not resolved.
spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01: capabilities.storyboardQueue: true. No other field changed; cycle stays at 3.

Updated in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: binaries now reports six entries (piperCli/PIPER_PATH and piperModel/PIPER_MODEL_PATH joined the four media binaries), so a machine without Piper reports degraded exactly like one without the Whisper model; capabilities gained voiceQueue.
spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: capabilities.producer added. Reported from a probe of the Claude Code binary and never part of the ok/degraded decision.

endpoints.description: Lists every project directory under the configured media root, ascending by slug, with the five layout flags (raw, catalog, timeline, edl, out). Files and non-portable directory names are ignored silently; a missing media root answers an empty array.

responses.200: application/json: ProjectSummary[] = [{ slug, layout: { raw, catalog, timeline, edl, out } }] sorted ascending by slug. Empty array when the media root does not exist.
responses.500: INTERNAL_ERROR from the central error handler on a real storage failure. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Creates the canonical media project layout for a slug: raw/aroll, raw/broll, raw/images, raw/audio, raw/voice, raw/logo, work and out, in that order. Never touches an existing project.

request_body.schema: { slug: string } — unknown keys ignored, capped by RENDER_API_MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES

responses.201: application/json ProjectDetail with layout.catalog/timeline/edl false and assetCounts all zero, plus a location: /projects/<slug> header.
responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON — body is not a JSON object or slug is not a string. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: PROJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS — the directory already exists. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.413: REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID — slug breaks RN-2; no storage port was invoked. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-02: the layout gains raw/logo/, so a fresh project already has the directory the logo role uploads into and the producer skill writes to. Eight directories instead of seven.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, layout, assetSource: 'catalog' | 'raw-scan', assetCounts: { aroll, broll, image, audio, voice, logo } } — the six roles are always present.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: CATALOG_UNREADABLE or PROJECT_LAYOUT_INVALID. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Updated in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: assetCounts gained the voice key.
spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-02: assetCounts gains the logo key (additive). The catalog of @video-maker/auto-montage already classified raw/logo/ as role logo; countAssetsByRole was dropping it silently.

endpoints.description: Lists the raw assets of a project. work/catalog.json is the source of truth when it exists and validates (source: catalog, media from the catalog entry); otherwise a raw scan of raw/ answers with media null and probes nothing. A corrupt catalog never falls back to the raw scan.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, source: 'catalog' | 'raw-scan', assets: [{ path, role, fingerprint: { sizeBytes, modifiedAtMs }, media: MediaAsset | null }], probeFailures: [{ path, errorCode }] } — probeFailures never carries the engine message.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: CATALOG_UNREADABLE (catalog present but unreadable) or PROJECT_LAYOUT_INVALID (raw/ missing on a raw scan). application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Uploads one raw asset as a raw binary body (never multipart) into raw/<rawDirectoryForRole(role)>/<filename>, writing to work/.uploads and promoting it with a rename, then probing it and merging the entry into work/catalog.json within the same request. A failed probe keeps the file and records the failure in the catalog. The role segment accepts the six roles of the catalog: aroll, broll, image, audio, voice and logo.

request_body.schema: raw binary body, capped by RENDER_API_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES

responses.201: application/json: the catalog entry just written { path, role, fingerprint, media } plus a location: /projects/<slug>/files/raw/<dir>/<filename> header.
responses.400: ASSET_CONTENT_TYPE_REQUIRED or ASSET_UPLOAD_ABORTED — nothing was promoted. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS — the destination exists; the temporary is removed. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.411: ASSET_CONTENT_LENGTH_REQUIRED. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.413: ASSET_TOO_LARGE — rejected from the content-length header before the first byte. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, ASSET_ROLE_INVALID (expected: 'aroll, broll, image, audio, voice or logo') or ASSET_PATH_INVALID — no storage port was invoked. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: CATALOG_UNREADABLE (assetPersisted true, catalogUpdated false), MEDIA_COMMAND_FAILED or MEDIA_OUTPUT_UNPARSEABLE (assetPersisted true, catalogUpdated true). application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.503: MEDIA_BINARY_NOT_FOUND with assetPersisted true and catalogUpdated true. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Updated in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: the role path segment accepts 'voice', which stores under raw/voice/ and only admits audio extensions; a video uploaded with that role is ignored by the catalog as extension-role-mismatch.

spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-02: the role path segment accepts 'logo', which stores under raw/logo/ and only admits image extensions (extension-role-mismatch otherwise). Without it the Show logo control of the Web Studio would have no way to get a logo into the project.

responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

responses.200: application/json: the EditDecisionList document as stored.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND or EDL_NOT_FOUND. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Streams any project artifact under raw/, work/ or out/ as raw bytes, served by the process itself instead of a signed URL. Content type comes from a closed extension table and a single-range Range header is honoured. This route never parses the file content.

responses.200: the file bytes with content-type from the extension table, content-length and accept-ranges: bytes — also for a malformed or multi-range Range header.
responses.206: the requested bytes with content-range: bytes <start>-<end>/<size> and the narrowed content-length.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND when the path is absent or is a directory (no directory listing). application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.416: RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE with a content-range: bytes */<size> header. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, or ASSET_PATH_INVALID for a non-portable path or one outside raw/, work/ and out/. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

endpoints.description: Creates a job for the project — render (default), montage or storyboard, selected by an optional kind field in the request body. kind absent, an empty body, or a body without a kind field all mean render, byte for byte identical to before this cycle: no request body was ever read for this endpoint prior to spec-e-burgos-007. render: the stored Timeline is read from work/timeline.json, validated and snapshotted once at creation, so a job always renders the Timeline that existed when it was created and never a later PUT. montage: runs ingestProject then autoMontage from @video-maker/auto-montage over media/<slug>/ with preset (default software-demo) and seed (default 0), rejected with 409 if work/timeline.json already exists unless overwrite: true is sent. The job id is generated by the service; for render it is the same id used for out/<id>.mp4 and work/renders/<id>/. Dispatch is FIFO with concurrency 1 across both kinds: the job is born running when the single slot is free and queued otherwise. storyboard: asks the AI agent (the local claude CLI, no API key) for a storyboard and writes work/storyboard.json. It takes exactly one of brief (an idea to turn into a script) or scriptText (an already written script to split into scenes) — neither or both is STORYBOARD_INPUT_INVALID — and is rejected with 409 if work/storyboard.json already exists unless overwrite: true is sent. Its stages are collect (project inventory: catalog assets, A-roll transcript, previous storyboard), propose (the agent call) and persist. spec-e-burgos-014 cycle-01: montage also accepts scriptPath XOR scriptText (the script the voice reads, used to align the captions word by word against it keeping the whisper timings) and logo: 'auto' | 'off' (default auto: if raw/logo/ has an image it becomes the logo layer of the Timeline, bottom-right). Its report gains logoAssetId and scriptAlignment { replaced, removed, inserted, dropped, corrected }. FIX-e-burgos-008-001: storyboard and voice accept an optional model validated against the PRODUCER_MODELS list of the studio producer, so the chat can run a job with the model of the turn; CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL (default sonnet) is the fallback and the agent is never invoked without --model. FIX-e-burgos-007-001: montage accepts format (the OutputPreset of the Timeline, default reels-9x16) and forwards it to autoMontage as outputPreset. FIX-e-burgos-009-001: voice accepts scriptText XOR scriptPath (one sentence per line) as an alternative to the storyboard, plus gapMs (default 900): it synthesizes one wav per sentence, concatenates them with that silence into work/voice/voice.wav (48 kHz mono), transcribes it into work/voice/voice.words.json and writes work/voice/script-manifest.json with source: 'script'. The job report gains source ('storyboard' | 'script'), a nullable storyboardId and a nullable track { path, wordsPath, durationMs, lineCount, gapMs }.

request_body.schema: { kind?: 'render' | 'montage' | 'storyboard' | 'voice', preset?: string, seed?: number, overwrite?: boolean, scriptPath?: string, scriptText?: string, logo?: 'auto' | 'off', brief?: string, voice?: string, sceneIds?: string[], gapMs?: number, model?: string, format?: 'reels-9x16' | 'tiktok-9x16' | 'shorts-9x16' | 'youtube-16x9' } — every field optional; preset/seed/scriptPath/scriptText/logo are read only when kind is 'montage', brief/scriptText only when kind is 'storyboard', voice/sceneIds/gapMs only when kind is 'voice' (and scriptText/scriptPath are read by 'voice' too, as the alternative to the storyboard), overwrite by montage, storyboard and voice, format only when kind is 'montage', and model by storyboard and voice (validated against PRODUCER_MODELS; storyboard passes it to the CLI as --model, voice accepts it for uniformity and ignores it).

responses.202: application/json: the full Job — { id, kind, slug, state, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt, progress, report, error } — with a location: /jobs/<id> header. 202 and not 201: the job resource exists and is queryable immediately, the deliverable does not.
responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON when a body is sent and is not syntactically valid JSON (new in this cycle: previously any body was ignored unread). No job is registered. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND when the project root is missing or is not a directory, or (kind: render only) TIMELINE_NOT_FOUND when work/timeline.json is absent. No job is registered in either case. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. MONTAGE_SCRIPT_NOT_FOUND (kind: montage) is surfaced when the async job settles, not at request time, if scriptPath does not resolve to a readable file inside the project. VOICE_SCRIPT_NOT_FOUND (kind: voice) is surfaced when the async job settles, not at request time, if scriptPath does not resolve to a readable file inside the project.
responses.409: TIMELINE_ALREADY_EXISTS (kind: montage) when work/timeline.json already exists and overwrite is not true, or STORYBOARD_ALREADY_EXISTS (kind: storyboard) when work/storyboard.json already exists and overwrite is not true. No job is registered and no file is touched. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. VOICE_ALREADY_EXISTS (kind: voice, script mode) when work/voice/voice.wav already exists and overwrite is not true.
responses.413: REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE when a body is sent and exceeds the shared JSON body limit (new in this cycle: previously any body was ignored unread). No job is registered. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID for a slug that is not a single kebab-case path segment; JOB_KIND_INVALID when kind is present and neither 'render' nor 'montage'; (kind: render only) TIMELINE_INVALID when the stored document does not parse or validate; (kind: montage only) MONTAGE_PRESET_INVALID, MONTAGE_SEED_INVALID, MONTAGE_OVERWRITE_INVALID for an invalid parameter, or MONTAGE_RAW_MISSING (surfaced when the async job settles, not at request time) when raw/ has no role directory. No job is registered for any of the request-time codes. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. STORYBOARD_INPUT_INVALID (kind: storyboard) when brief and scriptText are both absent, both present, or not a non-empty string; STORYBOARD_OVERWRITE_INVALID when overwrite is not a boolean; JOB_KIND_INVALID now names 'render', 'montage' or 'storyboard'. No job is registered. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }. MONTAGE_SCRIPT_INVALID (kind: montage) when scriptPath and scriptText are both present or either is not a non-empty string; MONTAGE_LOGO_INVALID when logo is neither 'auto' nor 'off'. No job is registered for either. JOB_MODEL_INVALID (kind: storyboard or voice) when model is present and is not one of PRODUCER_MODELS; no job is registered. MONTAGE_FORMAT_INVALID (kind: montage) when format is present and is not one of the four output presets; no job is registered. VOICE_SCRIPT_INVALID (kind: voice) when scriptText and scriptPath are both present, either is not a non-empty string, sceneIds comes together with a script, or gapMs is not a non-negative integer or arrives without a script; no job is registered.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

changelog.change: Adds an optional kind: 'render' | 'montage' discriminant to the request body (default render, fully backward compatible with the previously-unread body, spec-e-burgos-007 D-2). kind: 'montage' accepts preset/seed/overwrite, runs ingestProject + autoMontage, and can answer 409 TIMELINE_ALREADY_EXISTS or 422 for an invalid parameter. Reading the body at all is new for this endpoint and adds 400 REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON and 413 REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE for a malformed or oversized body; an absent body keeps the previous behaviour byte for byte. The response Job gains a kind field; every field already published for a render job keeps its name, type and meaning.

spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01: third job kind 'storyboard' with brief XOR scriptText and overwrite; new 409 STORYBOARD_ALREADY_EXISTS and 422 STORYBOARD_INPUT_INVALID / STORYBOARD_OVERWRITE_INVALID. Every field already published keeps its name, type and meaning.

Updated in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: accepts kind: 'voice' with the optional parameters voice (a voice id from GET /voices), sceneIds (regenerate only those scenes) and overwrite. The storyboard must exist (404 STORYBOARD_NOT_FOUND), every sceneId must be one of its scenes (404 VOICE_SCENE_NOT_FOUND) and a scene that already has a track needs overwrite: true (409 VOICE_ALREADY_EXISTS); the three are evaluated before the job is registered. Stages are synthesize | transcribe | persist with a per-scene counter. JOB_KIND_INVALID now names the four valid kinds.

Updated in spec-e-burgos-014 cycle-01: kind: 'montage' accepts scriptPath XOR scriptText and logo: 'auto' | 'off'. New 422 MONTAGE_SCRIPT_INVALID and MONTAGE_LOGO_INVALID at request time, and 404 MONTAGE_SCRIPT_NOT_FOUND when the job settles. The montage report gains logoAssetId (string | null) and scriptAlignment ({ replaced, removed, inserted, dropped, corrected } | null). Every field already published keeps its name, type and meaning; a body without the new fields behaves exactly as before.

FIX-e-burgos-008-001: kind 'storyboard' and kind 'voice' accept an optional model, validated against PRODUCER_MODELS, with 422 JOB_MODEL_INVALID and no job registered when it is not on the list. The storyboard job passes it to the claude CLI as --model (CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL, default sonnet, is the fallback); the voice job accepts it for uniformity and ignores it. AI_AGENT_FAILED now carries the provider detail in subtype and result (600 chars each) and a hint naming 'claude update' when the CLI is too old. A body without model behaves exactly as before.

FIX-e-burgos-007-001: kind 'montage' accepts an optional format — one of reels-9x16 (default), tiktok-9x16, shorts-9x16, youtube-16x9 — passed to autoMontage as outputPreset and written into timeline.format. 422 MONTAGE_FORMAT_INVALID and no job registered for any other value. The default is deliberately fixed rather than derived from the A-roll orientation, so a body without format behaves exactly as before.

FIX-e-burgos-009-001: kind 'voice' accepts scriptText XOR scriptPath and gapMs (default 900) as an alternative input to the storyboard, and writes work/voice/voice.wav + work/voice/voice.words.json + work/voice/script-manifest.json (source: 'script') without touching the storyboard manifest. New 422 VOICE_SCRIPT_INVALID and 404 VOICE_SCRIPT_NOT_FOUND, and 409 VOICE_ALREADY_EXISTS now also guards work/voice/voice.wav. BREAKING for a reader of the voice job report: it gains source and track and storyboardId becomes nullable; apps/web was updated in the same fix.

endpoints.description: Lists the project's jobs (render and montage) in creation order, each reduced to a summary (id, kind, state, stage, errorCode, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt) — never the full report or the full error, which GET /jobs/:jobId serves. The listing is scoped strictly by slug and does not check that the project exists on disk.

responses.200: application/json: { slug: string, jobs: [{ id, kind, state, stage, errorCode, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt }] }. A slug with no jobs answers an empty jobs array, whether or not the project exists.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID for a slug that is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

changelog.change: Each summary gains a kind: 'render' | 'montage' field; every field already published (id, state, stage, errorCode, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt) keeps its name, type and meaning for render jobs.

endpoints.description: Full detail of a single job (render or montage) in any of its six states (queued, running, canceling, succeeded, failed, canceled). The job id is globally unique because the queue is global, not per project, so no slug is required. The lookup is an in-memory Map read, never a filesystem access, so the id is not validated as a path segment. progress carries the current stage: for kind 'render', monotonic renderedFrames/totalFrames/percent during the render stage only; for kind 'montage', monotonic processedAssets/totalAssets/percent during the probe and transcribe stages only (discover and plan never carry a count).

responses.200: application/json: the full Job. Also 200 for state: 'failed' — the job's own failure is not a transport error and the typed error is embedded in the body instead of becoming the response status.
responses.404: RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND for an id the queue does not know, including one lost to a process restart (the queue is in memory and does not persist). application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

changelog.change: Adds a kind: 'render' | 'montage' field. For kind: 'montage', progress uses its own stage set (discover/probe/transcribe/plan) and counter field names (processedAssets/totalAssets instead of renderedFrames/totalFrames), and report uses MontageJobReport (catalogPath, timelinePath, editDecisionListPath, preset, seed) instead of RenderPipelineReport. Every field already published for kind: 'render' keeps its name, type and meaning.

endpoints.description: Requests cancellation of a job (render or montage). Cancellation is real but cooperative: no process is ever signalled or killed. A queued job is canceled immediately without invoking a single pipeline port. A running job moves to the observable transitional state canceling and settles as canceled at the next stage checkpoint (for montage: only before ingestProject starts or before autoMontage starts — never mid-way through either opaque call), after the binary in flight finishes its current invocation. A job canceled while its last stage is in flight still settles as canceled with report: null even though its on-disk artifacts (out/<jobId>.mp4 for render; work/catalog.json for montage) may already exist and be complete — the entry state wins over the pipeline result. Nothing on disk is ever deleted.

responses.200: application/json: the full Job with state: 'canceled', for a job that was queued. Terminal and done.
responses.202: application/json: the full Job with state: 'canceling', for a job that was running — accepted, still in flight. Repeating the request on an already canceling job answers 202 again, idempotently, and is never a 409.
responses.404: RENDER_JOB_NOT_FOUND for an id the queue does not know. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: RENDER_JOB_NOT_CANCELABLE for a job already in a terminal state (succeeded, failed or canceled). Its final state is never changed. application/json: { error: { code, stage: null, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: application/json: { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', stage: null, message } } from the central error handler.

changelog.change: Cancellation now applies with the identical cooperative semantics to kind: 'montage' jobs; no field or status code changes for kind: 'render'.

endpoints.description: Returns the storyboard document persisted at work/storyboard.json, validated against StoryboardDocumentSchema (@video-maker/timeline-core) on read. The document carries the title, language, aspect ratio, the character sheet whose visual descriptions keep a character consistent across separately generated shots, the project-wide caption style and music tags, and the ordered scenes. Each scene carries its narration, the visual prompt the user pastes into an external generative tool, the visual source (upload | asset | remotion-scene), the optional catalog assetId or native Remotion scene (title | text | code | image-kenburns) with its props, an estimated duration, an optional per-scene caption style, and its music and sfx tags.

responses.200: application/json: the full StoryboardDocument — { schemaVersion, id, source, createdAt, title, language, format, captionsStyle, musicTags, characters[], scenes[] }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND when the project root is missing or is not a directory, or STORYBOARD_NOT_FOUND when work/storyboard.json is absent. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case segment, or STORYBOARD_INVALID when the stored file is not valid JSON or does not pass StoryboardDocumentSchema. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01: storyboard document endpoints of the generative mode.

endpoints.description: Replaces the storyboard document of the project. The body is validated against StoryboardDocumentSchema BEFORE the project is resolved, so an invalid document is rejected without touching the disk, and it is persisted with serializeMontageDocument from @video-maker/auto-montage, the same writer used for timeline.json and edl.json, so the bytes match what the rest of work/ produces. This is how a hand edit survives: a storyboard job refuses to overwrite an existing document unless overwrite: true is sent.

request_body.schema: A full StoryboardDocument accepted by StoryboardDocumentSchema. Partial documents are rejected: the write is a replacement, never a merge.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, path } where path is the project-relative work/storyboard.json.
responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON when the body is absent, empty or not syntactically valid JSON. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND when the project root is missing or is not a directory. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.413: REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE when the body exceeds the shared JSON body limit. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, or STORYBOARD_INVALID when the document does not pass StoryboardDocumentSchema. No file is written. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01: storyboard document endpoints of the generative mode.

endpoints.description: Returns the visual prompts of the storyboard as plain text, ready to copy into an external generative tool (Meta AI, Google Flow). The character sheet comes first, so the user can paste a character description together with the prompt of any shot it appears in. Then one block per scene, numbered from 01 with the scene index and annotated with its visual source, so the file the user brings back can be named by number (01.mp4, 03.png) for the batch import of spec-e-burgos-010. Scenes that need no external footage are listed too: skipping them would break that numbering.

responses.200: text/plain; charset=utf-8 with an explicit content-length: the numbered prompt sheet.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or STORYBOARD_NOT_FOUND when the project has no storyboard to export. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, or STORYBOARD_INVALID when the stored document does not pass validation. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-008 cycle-01: storyboard document endpoints of the generative mode.

endpoints.description: Lists the Piper voice models installed on the machine. The list is derived from the .onnx files sitting next to the model configured in PIPER_MODEL_PATH, so dropping a new voice in that directory is enough to make it selectable; the .onnx.json config files are not voices and are filtered out. It is a resource of its own and not a field of GET /health because health is polled and must not pay a directory read per call. The route is not project-scoped: voices belong to the machine, not to a project.

responses.200: application/json: { voices: [{ id, fileName, isDefault }] } sorted by id. id is the file name without its .onnx extension and is what a voice job accepts in its voice parameter. isDefault marks the model configured in PIPER_MODEL_PATH. An empty array means the directory has no .onnx model.
responses.503: VOICE_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE when PIPER_MODEL_PATH is not set or does not point at a readable file. Answering an empty list there would be a lie: the difference between 'no voices installed' and 'Piper not configured' is what the studio needs to explain. The payload never carries the resolved path of the voice directory. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: catalog of locally installed Piper voices.

endpoints.description: Returns the voice manifest of the project (work/voice/manifest.json) plus a per-track staleness view computed against the stored storyboard. The manifest is the source of truth for the real duration of every scene: durationMs is measured with ffprobe on the mixable wav and supersedes the estimatedDurationMs the model proposed. The wav and the words document of each track are served by EP-011 under their project-relative paths.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, manifest, scenes }. manifest is a document accepted by VoiceManifestSchema: { schemaVersion, storyboardId, language, tracks: [{ sceneId, index, source, path, wordsPath, durationMs, sampleRate, voiceId, narrationHash, updatedAt }] }, tracks ordered by scene index. scenes carries one { sceneId, index, source, stale } per track: stale is true when the narration of that scene changed after the track was produced, and null when the scene is no longer in the storyboard or the storyboard is unreadable.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, or VOICE_NOT_FOUND when the project has no manifest yet (no voice job has run and no locution was attached). application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, or VOICE_INVALID when the stored manifest does not pass VoiceManifestSchema. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: voice manifest of the generative mode.

endpoints.description: Attaches a locution the user recorded to one scene of the storyboard. The file must already be under raw/voice/ (uploaded with EP-006 and the voice role); this endpoint only names it. The file is normalized to the sample rate of the mix and transcribed with the same Whisper the ingest uses, so an uploaded track carries word timings exactly like a synthesized one, and its entry lands in the manifest with source: 'uploaded' and voiceId: null. A later voice job never replaces an uploaded track, which is how RF-7 is enforced: the recorded locution wins over the synthesized one. The call is synchronous and runs ffmpeg and whisper-cli inline, so a long take holds the connection: turning it into a fourth job kind is a decision left to a future cycle.

request_body.schema: { fileName } where fileName is a portable file name (no separators, no parent segments) already present under raw/voice/ of this project.

responses.200: application/json: { slug, path, track } where path is the project-relative work/voice/manifest.json and track is the VoiceTrack that was stored, with source 'uploaded', voiceId null and the durationMs measured with ffprobe.
responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON when the body is absent, empty, not valid JSON or not a JSON object. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, STORYBOARD_NOT_FOUND when there is no storyboard to attach the locution to, VOICE_SCENE_NOT_FOUND when the sceneId is not one of its scenes, or VOICE_ASSET_NOT_FOUND when the named file is not a file under raw/voice/. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.413: REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE when the body exceeds the shared JSON body limit. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID, or ASSET_PATH_INVALID when fileName is missing, is not a string or would escape raw/voice/. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.500: VOICE_TRANSCRIPTION_FAILED when ffmpeg or whisper-cli fails while normalizing or aligning the take. The manifest is left untouched. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.503: VOICE_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE when the whisper binary or its model does not resolve. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-009 cycle-01: attach an uploaded locution to a storyboard scene.

endpoints.description: Returns the whole producer conversation of the project, the Claude Code session that backs it and the turn in flight if there is one. This is what the studio chat screen loads when it opens. The conversation is persisted in media/<slug>/work/producer/conversation.json (and mirrored, human readable, in conversation.md), so it survives a restart of the service: the queue does not. The catalog of models the user can choose from travels with the conversation: default is PRODUCER_MODEL and allowed is PRODUCER_MODELS (FIX-e-burgos-015-001).

responses.200: application/json: { slug, messages: [{ id, role: user|assistant, text, createdAt, suggestions?: string[], turnId?, model? }], session: { sessionId, model, createdAt, lastTurnAt } | null, activeTurn: ProducerTurn | null, models: { default: string, allowed: [{ id, label, description }] } }. messages is [] and session is null for a project that never talked to the producer; model is filled on the assistant messages and carries the model that produced the answer. session.model is the model in effect for the next turn and models.allowed is the closed list POST .../producer/messages accepts. activeTurn carries the same shape as EP-024 and is null unless a turn is running.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND when the project directory does not exist. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment, PRODUCER_STATE_INVALID when conversation.json or session.json exist but cannot be read (the service refuses to overwrite a conversation it cannot parse). application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: conversation, session and active turn of the studio producer.
Added models: { default, allowed: [{ id, label, description }] } and model on each assistant message, so the chat can offer the model picker and show which model wrote each answer.

endpoints.description: Sends one user message to the producer and starts a turn. The turn runs OUTSIDE the job queue (D-1 of the cycle): the agent enqueues montage/render jobs on this same API and waits for them, so a turn sitting in a queue of concurrency 1 would deadlock itself. Exclusion is per project: one running turn per slug. The user message is persisted before the 202 answers, so the chat can render it immediately. Cancellation kills the child process (it is not the cooperative cancellation of the job queue). The model of the turn is chosen per message: model is optional and validated against PRODUCER_MODELS; when it is absent the service keeps the model of the session and falls back to PRODUCER_MODEL. The model in effect is persisted in session.json, and switching model on a later turn is supported (claude -p --resume <id> --model <m>).

request_body.schema: { text: string, model?: string } — text is the user message, non-empty after trimming; model is one of the aliases of GET .../producer models.allowed. Any other field is ignored.

responses.202: application/json: { slug, turnId, startedAt, status: running }. Poll EP-024 for the events and the answer.
responses.400: REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON when the body is absent, empty or not a JSON object. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.404: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND when the project directory does not exist. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: PRODUCER_TURN_ACTIVE when the project already has a running turn; resource carries its turnId. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.413: REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE when the body exceeds the JSON body limit. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PRODUCER_MESSAGE_INVALID when text is missing or blank, PRODUCER_MODEL_INVALID when model is present and is not one of the allowed models (resource carries the rejected value, expected the allowed list; the turn is not reserved), PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.503: PRODUCER_UNAVAILABLE when the Claude Code binary does not resolve or the video-producer skill file cannot be read. Checked before the turn is reserved, so a 503 never leaves the project blocked. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: one producer turn per project, outside the job queue.
Accepts an optional model in the body, validated against PRODUCER_MODELS (422 PRODUCER_MODEL_INVALID), passed to claude --model and persisted in session.json.

endpoints.description: Returns the state of one producer turn: its accumulated events while it runs, and its answer plus suggestions when it succeeds. Events are derived from the stream-json output of Claude Code at message granularity (no partial chunks, D-3): a text block becomes a text event, a tool call becomes a tool event with a readable summary built from the command itself, and a failed tool result becomes a status event. The raw stream is kept, one JSON per line, in work/producer/turns/<turnId>.jsonl.

responses.200: application/json: { turnId, slug, status: running|succeeded|failed|canceled, model, startedAt, finishedAt: string|null, events: ({ type: text, text } | { type: tool, name, summary } | { type: status, status })[], assistantMessage: string|null, suggestions: string[], error: ErrorPayload|null }. model is the model the turn actually ran with. assistantMessage is the answer with the ```suggestions block removed; suggestions holds 2 to 4 short actions taken from that block ([] when the model did not emit one). error is filled only when status is failed.
responses.404: PRODUCER_TURN_NOT_FOUND when the turn id is unknown or belongs to another project. The registry lives in memory: a turn from a previous run of the service answers the same 404. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: state, events, answer and suggestions of a producer turn.
The turn record reports the model it ran with; EP-025 answers the same record.

endpoints.description: Cancels a running producer turn by killing its child process (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period). Unlike a job, there is no cooperative checkpoint to wait for: the agent is an opaque external process. The answer is 202 because the turn settles when the process actually dies; poll EP-024 until status is canceled. A canceled turn persists neither an assistant message nor a session, so the next turn starts a fresh Claude Code session unless an earlier turn already created one.

responses.202: application/json: the turn record of EP-024, still status running at the moment the kill was requested.
responses.404: PRODUCER_TURN_NOT_FOUND when the turn id is unknown or belongs to another project. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.409: PRODUCER_TURN_NOT_CANCELABLE when the turn already reached succeeded, failed or canceled. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.
responses.422: PROJECT_SLUG_INVALID when the slug is not a single kebab-case path segment. application/json: { error: { code, stage, message, resource?, expected?, hint?, assetPersisted?, catalogUpdated? } }.

changelog.change: Created in spec-e-burgos-015 cycle-01: kill of the producer child process.
